tier_rationale: A traditional key-wound mechanical alarm clock: the movement and the bell alarm are both driven entirely by a wound spring. The manufacturer's own instruction manual states plainly, 'Your clock does not require batteries or electricity to operate,' and documents only mechanical controls -- a time winding key, an alarm winding key, an alarm on/off slide switch, and a mechanical +/- regulator lever -- with no battery compartment, cord, or electronic component anywhere. A device with no electrical power source at all cannot contain an intentional radiator, so this is the clearest possible D0: no radio because there is no electronics to hold one.
the_unplug_test: There is no router to unplug and nothing to notice its absence. The clock keeps time and rings its bell alarm purely from a wound mainspring; you rewind it by hand every day or two. It has worked exactly the same way, with no changes possible, since the day it was made.

repairability.notes: Purely mechanical movement; no batteries to replace. Clock and watch repair shops service key-wound movements, though this is not a manufacturer-documented user repair.

sources.supports: Official Westclox 'Instructions & Warranty' manual for Model# 15550 / 15550CN, warranty administered by NYL Holdings LLC (the current owner of the Westclox brand). States directly under Time Wind-Up: 'Your clock does not require batteries or electricity to operate.' Documents the fully mechanical operation: a wound time spring runs the movement for at least 24 hours, a separate alarm winding key powers the bell alarm, and a mechanical +/- regulator lever adjusts timekeeping accuracy -- no battery compartment, cord, or electronic component described anywhere in the instructions.

Independent hardware-store retail listing for the same model 15550, corroborating: 'it requires no batteries or electric power to keep time,' key-wound mechanism, independent alarm indicator, luminous hands, priced $17.44 with no sold-out notice.

open_questions: Real-time stock status varies by retailer (sold out at the Westclox-authorized store, apparently available at McCoy's at time of check) -- worth re-checking before publishing to confirm current purchasability.

No FCC search was run for this model since a device with no battery compartment or power source cannot contain an intentional radiator; this is treated as self-evident rather than requiring a grantee search.
notes: First record in the empty 'alarm clock' subcategory. Chosen over a quartz/electronic alarm clock because it is unambiguous: no power source at all, not merely no radio.
